notes:
Summary: Gullstrand is a government-flagged naval dockworks contractor evaluating Redwood Private for shipyard operational assistants and document search inside an air-gapped environment. Primary drivers: remove manual sifting of maintenance logs, accelerate engineering triage, automated incident summarization for shift handover.

Constraints / must-haves: full air-gap (no internet egress), SCIF-style HSM/KMS for keys, SSO/SAML with their IdP bridging, long-term audit logging (7+ years), data residency to on-prem vaults, and ITAR export controls. They explicitly said: 'If the model ever leaves site we can't proceed.'

PoC scope definition (draft): deploy Redwood Private control plane on isolated subnet, single-model LLM (quantized) tuned for maintenance docs, enable local embeddings store for search, integrate with existing CMDB and shipyard ticketing. Provide on-site install guide and operator runbook.

Commercial: prefer capex + 12 month support. Budget roughly in range $250k–$1M subject to SOW. Procurement lead expects procurement package to go to gate review in June.

Call notes / quotes: 'We need deterministic behavior during shift turnovers' — Captain R. Hennings (ops lead). SE asks to confirm acceptable latency floor: 200–400ms token latency for internal chat workflows; bulk embedding jobs can be scheduled off-peak.

Security interactions: security team has started a gap analysis vs their checklist; they flagged need for FIPS-validated crypto and HSM attestation. Redwood to propose HSM/KMS integration approach and provide sample audit log schema.

Next immediate actions: (1) Redwood SE to produce PoC hardware + install checklist (due 2026-03-12); (2) Redwood security to supply SOC2 excerpts + integration notes (SEC-2987); (3) schedule 2-day on-site install window for air-gapped PoC (customer requested week of 2026-03-17).
